In [[group theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], '''Frattini's argument''' is an important [[Lemma (mathematics)|lemma]] in the structure theory of [[finite group]]s.  It is named after [[Giovanni Frattini]], who used it in a paper from 1885 when defining the [[Frattini subgroup]] of a group. The argument was taken by Frattini, as he himself admits, from a paper of [[Alfredo Capelli]] dated 1884.<ref>M. Brescia, F. de Giovanni, M. Trombetti, [http://www.advgrouptheory.com/journal/Volumes/3/M.%20Brescia,%20F.%20de%20Giovanni,%20M.%20Trombetti%20-%20The%20true%20story%20behind%20Frattinis%20Argument.pdf "The True Story Behind Frattini’s Argument"], ''[[Advances in Group Theory and Applications]]'' '''3''', [https://doi.org/10.4399/97888255036928 doi:10.4399/97888255036928]</ref>

==Frattini's argument==
===Statement===

If <math>G</math> is a finite group with normal subgroup <math>H</math>, and if <math>P</math> is a [[Sylow p-subgroup|Sylow ''p''-subgroup]] of <math>H</math>, then

: <math>G = N_G(P)H,</math>

where <math>N_G(P)</math> denotes the [[centralizer and normalizer|normalizer]] of <math>P</math> in <math>G</math>, and <math>N_G(P)H</math> means the [[product of group subsets]].

===Proof===
The group <math>P</math> is a Sylow <math>p</math>-subgroup of <math>H</math>, so every Sylow <math>p</math>-subgroup of <math>H</math> is an <math>H</math>-conjugate of <math>P</math>, that is, it is of the form <math>h^{-1}Ph</math> for some <math>h \in H</math> (see [[Sylow theorems]]).  Let <math>g</math> be any element of <math>G</math>. Since <math>H</math> is normal in <math>G</math>, the subgroup <math>g^{-1}Pg</math> is contained in <math>H</math>. This means that <math>g^{-1}Pg</math> is a Sylow <math>p</math>-subgroup of <math>H</math>. Then, by the above, it must be <math>H</math>-conjugate to <math>P</math>: that is, for some <math>h \in H</math>

: <math>g^{-1}Pg = h^{-1}Ph,</math>

and so
  
: <math>hg^{-1}Pgh^{-1} = P.</math>

Thus

: <math>gh^{-1} \in N_G(P),</math>

and therefore <math>g \in N_G(P)H</math>. But <math>g \in G</math> was arbitrary, and so <math>G = HN_G(P) = N_G(P)H.\ \square</math>

==Applications==
* Frattini's argument can be used as part of a proof that any finite [[nilpotent group]] is a [[direct product of groups|direct product]] of its Sylow subgroups.
* By applying Frattini's argument to <math>N_G(N_G(P))</math>, it can be shown that <math>N_G(N_G(P)) = N_G(P)</math> whenever <math>G</math> is a finite group and <math>P</math> is a Sylow <math>p</math>-subgroup of <math>G</math>.
* More generally, if a subgroup <math>M  \leq G</math> contains <math>N_G(P)</math> for some Sylow <math>p</math>-subgroup <math>P</math> of <math>G</math>, then <math>M</math> is self-normalizing, i.e. <math>M = N_G(M)</math>.
